newsitem.title: POLAND: Shareholders cut size of Agros issue.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders cut size of Agros issue.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish food trader and producer Agros Holding SA on Friday approved a plan to issue 2,425,000 new shares, cutting the size of the issue from the 3,425,000 shares proposed by the executive board.
In mid-October the Agros holding company's board proposed the ex-rights issue, in three separate batches directed at existing shareholders, selected large investors and the general public.
The extraordinary shareholders' meeting on Friday approved these principles of the issue but reduced its scale.
Executive vice-president Marek Gucik said that Agros aimed to use proceeds from the issue to improve productivity of the holding's firms and for investment in food sector operations.

"The investment programme will improve productivity of the holding's firms, strengthen its position on the juices and drinks market, expand the offer of food products...and allow equity investment in new firms by obtaining strategic stakes," Gucik said.
He said the aim was to strengthen Agros' position in areas where it was already present and help it enter new market segments such as oils, grain and milling and confectionery.
Agros President Zofia Gaber said after the meeting that the reduction of the issue's size was not a serious problem but might mean some investments would have to be reduced or delayed.
"We see no great drama in this. Some projects will probably have to be delayed," she told Reuters.

"We are approaching the first stage of implementing our goals, and we don't have to decide in advance how the second stage will be financed -- it could be from credits or maybe, with time, we will return to our proposal to increase share capital," Gaber said.
Agros shares rose 7.4 percent on Friday to 68 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse.
